title: Humans or LLMs as the Judge? A Study on Judgement Bias

paper.authors: Chen, Chen, Liu, Zhou, Xiao, Wang, Zhu, Wan, Li, Wang (FreedomIntelligence)
paper.repo_commit: fbd30c9b0d2e204fbfe925bc77f26b9a30a5b5b9 (clone external/repos/W4404782878/FreedomIntelligence__Humans_LLMs_Judgement_Bias; PDF link was glued as ..._Biasbenchmarks). Data only - no code.

dependence.note: LLMs act as pairwise judges of answer quality; the metric (ASR) is the fraction of judge preferences that flip under perturbations. Answers themselves were generated by gpt-4-0613 (temperature 0.5) and are fixed in the released data.

claim.statement: LLM judges' preferences are shifted by perturbations of the compared answer: in Table 1, GPT-4o (best judge) has ASR 0.06 (factual error), 0.16 (gender bias), 0.32 (fake reference), 0.07 (rich content), average rank 2.00; GPT-4-Turbo (gpt-4-1106-preview) 0.11 / 0.27 / 0.49 / 0.05; all judges except GPT-4o are no better than random (0.37) against fake references, and semantic-related biases are lower for strong LLMs than for humans (0.21 factual error).
claim.metric: Attack Success Rate (Sec. 4.6): share of samples whose aggregated preference moves toward the perturbed answer between control (A1 vs A2) and experimental (A1 vs A2^p) groups; 6 votes per pair aggregated as mean of {0, 0.5, 1} with threshold 0.5; Eq. 2 for reference/rich-content, Eq. 3 for factual error and gender

original_values.table5_positional_preference_GPT-4o: 0.427 / 0.333 / 0.240 / 0.186 (Answer1 / Answer2 / Tie / Diff columns as printed)

claim.original_source: Paper Table 1 (Sec. 5.2), Table 3 (Sec. 5.3), Table 4 (Appendix C model versions), Table 5 (Appendix F.1 positional bias)

params.temperature: not reported for judges (answers in data were generated at 0.5)

protocol.n_items: 142 questions (Bloom's-taxonomy levels, middle-school knowledge) x 5 groups = 710 pairs: control (A1 vs A2, data/raw.json) + 4 experimental (data/factual_error.json, gender.json, reference.json, rich_content.json; 142 records each, JSON-lines)
protocol.samples_per_item: 6 votes per pair (Fig. 2); for LLM judges presumably 3 prompt variants x 2 answer orders - composition not stated explicitly
protocol.evaluation: Automatic once votes exist: parse vote, map to {0, 0.5, 1}, average 6 votes, threshold 0.5, compute ASR per perturbation (Eqs. 2-3). No evaluation script released; ~30 lines to implement. Positional-bias screen (Table 5) should be recomputed first, as the paper excludes judges that fail it.
protocol.environment_check: Verify the five JSON-lines files load (142 records each; keys question_id, question, prompt, model_id, temperature, answers{answer1, answer2, ...}) and that each experimental file carries the perturbed answer field before spending.

artifacts.data_path: data/raw.json (control), data/factual_error.json, data/gender.json, data/reference.json, data/rich_content.json (JSON-lines, 142 records each; answers generated by gpt-4 at temperature 0.5)
artifacts.notes: Judge prompts exist only in the paper appendix; human-judge votes and LLM-judge votes are not released, so original per-pair preferences cannot be inspected. Rich-content perturbation is Markdown that humans saw rendered; LLMs receive raw text.

budget.sampling_scheme: 6 votes per pair already built in (3 prompts x 2 orders); ANALYSIS_PLAN 3 seeds on top

full.note: gpt-4o: 710 pairs x 6 votes = 4,260 calls/seed x 3 seeds; ~700 input tokens (system prompt + question + two <=150-word answers), ~120 output avg (CoT variants ~200, direct ~5); ~23 USD/seed. Same design on gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 as a successor arm: ~45 USD/seed

representative_subset.note: already small; no subset needed. Minimal option: factual-error + fake-reference perturbations only (control + 2 groups = 426 pairs, ~14 USD/seed)

judgment.rule: ANALYSIS_PLAN Sec. 1 on GPT-4o's four ASR values: survival = each ASR within bootstrap 95% CI (over 142 questions) of the original and the two directional statements hold (semantic-related ASR <= 0.11 i.e. well below human 0.21; fake-reference ASR below random 0.37). Partial = ordering across perturbations preserved but one ASR leaves its CI. Dead = fake-reference ASR >= random or factual-error ASR exceeds humans.
judgment.notes: Binomial CI on 142 items is wide (+/- ~0.06 at p = 0.1), so judge on direction first.

triage_2026_09_18: Scoring defect fixed offline (no new calls): 354 of 4,260 judge replies in the 'direct' prompt variant were one-paragraph verdicts naming both answers and were dropped as unparsable; reading the verdict from the sentence subject (then a 'however/overall ... AnswerN' turn, then tie wording) recovers 334. ASR before -> after: factual_error: 0.069 -> 0.082 (paper 0.06) | gender: 0.111 -> 0.095 (paper 0.16) | reference: 0.371 -> 0.330 (paper 0.32) | rich_content: 0.323 -> 0.242 (paper 0.07). Verdict 사망 (death) -> 부분 생존 (partial). The remaining deviation is rich-content bias (paper 0.07): consistent across the three prompts, so it reads as a behavioural difference of the judge rather than scoring. result_before_triage.json / run_meta_before_triage.json keep the first pass.
